milestones.1: Engine: board model, validation, solving, generation, grading, hints
milestones.2: State: game store, undo/redo, persistence, timer
milestones.3: UI: playable game in the browser
milestones.4: Polish: accessibility, end-to-end coverage, docs, deploy

tasks.title: Playwright e2e harness with a smoke test
acceptance: @playwright/test is a devDependency; `npm run e2e` builds the app, serves it with `vite preview`, and runs Playwright against Chromium only
e2e/smoke.spec.ts loads the page and asserts the heading 'Sudoku' is visible
playwright.config.ts uses webServer so no manual server is needed
`npm run check` does not run e2e tests (vitest must not pick up e2e/)
CLAUDE.md commands section mentions `npx playwright install chromium` as a one-time setup step

tasks.title: ESLint and Prettier wired into npm run check
acceptance: ESLint flat config with typescript-eslint recommended rules; Prettier config with defaults plus printWidth 110
`npm run lint` runs eslint and `prettier --check`; `npm run format` writes fixes
`npm run check` runs typecheck, lint and test, and passes on the current tree
dist/, node_modules/ and director/ are ignored by both tools

tasks.title: Board model: types, parse/serialize, units and peers
acceptance: Exports a Grid type (81 cells, value 0 = empty, 1-9 digits) and helpers rowOf, colOf, boxOf, cellIndex
parseGrid accepts 81-char strings using '0' or '.' for blanks, ignores whitespace, and throws a descriptive error otherwise; serializeGrid returns the '.'-blank form
Precomputed UNITS (27) and PEERS (20 per cell) tables, verified by tests
Pure functions, no DOM; re-exported from src/engine/index.ts
Unit tests cover parsing round-trips and invalid input

tasks.title: Validator: conflicts and completion
acceptance: findConflicts(grid) returns the set of cell indices that share a digit with a peer
isComplete(grid) is true only for a full grid with no conflicts
isConsistentWith(grid, solution) reports cells whose value differs from the solution
Unit tests cover empty, partial, conflicting and solved grids

tasks.title: Solver: constraint propagation with backtracking and solution counting
acceptance: solve(grid) returns a solved Grid or null; it does not mutate its input
countSolutions(grid, limit = 2) stops early at the limit and is what uniqueness checks use
Uses candidate bitmasks with naked/hidden single propagation and minimum-remaining-values branching
Tests include at least 5 known puzzles (easy through 'hardest' class, e.g. Arto Inkala's) with known solutions, an unsolvable grid, and a multi-solution grid
Solves each of the hard test puzzles in under 50 ms in the vitest run (assert with a generous timer)
tasks.notes: Split into S tasks at setup to fit Pro 5-hour windows.

Tests: at least 3 known puzzles (easy to medium) with known solutions and an unsolvable grid

tasks.title: Solver: countSolutions and hard-puzzle tests with timing
acceptance: countSolutions(grid, limit = 2) stops early at the limit and is what uniqueness checks use
Tests add at least 2 'hardest'-class puzzles (e.g. Arto Inkala's) and a multi-solution grid
Solves each of the hard test puzzles in under 50 ms in the vitest run (assert with a generous timer)

tasks.title: Technique grader: human-style solver that rates difficulty
acceptance: Implements, as separate step functions, naked single, hidden single, naked pair/triple, hidden pair, pointing pair/box-line reduction, and X-wing
Each step returns a structured Step {technique, placements or eliminations, cells involved} usable later for hints
grade(grid) applies the easiest applicable technique repeatedly and returns {difficulty: 'easy'|'medium'|'hard'|'expert', hardestTechnique, steps}; 'expert' when the techniques cannot finish it
Difficulty mapping is documented in a comment table in grade.ts
Tests: one puzzle per technique where that technique is required, and grading of at least 4 reference puzzles
tasks.notes: Split into S tasks at setup to fit Pro 5-hour windows.

tasks.title: Technique steps: singles, naked pair/triple, hidden pair, pointing and box-line
acceptance: Implements naked single, hidden single, naked pair/triple, hidden pair, and pointing pair/box-line reduction as separate step functions
Each step returns a structured Step {technique, placements or eliminations, cells involved} usable later for hints
Tests: one puzzle or candidate state per technique where that technique is required

tasks.title: X-wing and grade(): difficulty rating from techniques
acceptance: Adds an X-wing step function in the same Step format, with a test that requires it
grade(grid) applies the easiest applicable technique repeatedly and returns {difficulty: 'easy'|'medium'|'hard'|'expert', hardestTechnique, steps}; 'expert' when the techniques cannot finish it
Difficulty mapping is documented in a comment table in grade.ts
Tests: grading of at least 4 reference puzzles

tasks.title: Generator: unique-solution puzzles at a requested difficulty
acceptance: Seedable PRNG in random.ts; generate({difficulty, seed}) is deterministic for a given seed
Builds a random full solution, then removes clues (symmetric by default) while countSolutions stays 1
Retries until grade() matches the requested difficulty, with a bounded attempt count, falling back to the closest grade found
Returns {puzzle, solution, difficulty, seed}
Tests: 20 seeded puzzles per difficulty all have exactly one solution and the requested (or documented fallback) grade; median generation time per easy/medium puzzle under 200 ms in Node
tasks.notes: Split into S tasks at setup to fit Pro 5-hour windows.

tasks.title: Generator core: seedable PRNG, random full solutions, unique-solution clue removal

generateUnique({seed}) returns {puzzle, solution, seed}; tests: 20 seeded puzzles all have exactly one solution

tasks.title: Generator: target a requested difficulty

Tests: 20 seeded puzzles per difficulty all have exactly one solution and the requested (or documented fallback) grade; median generation time per easy/medium puzzle under 200 ms in Node

tasks.title: Hint engine: next logical step for the player's current grid
acceptance: nextHint(grid, solution, notes?) returns {kind: 'mistake', cells} if any filled cell disagrees with the solution, otherwise the easiest technique Step that applies
Each hint carries a short plain-English explanation string, e.g. 'Only 7 fits in row 3'
Returns null on a solved grid
Tests cover mistake detection and at least three technique hints

tasks.title: Game state store: puzzle, entries, notes, selection
acceptance: GameState holds puzzle (givens), solution, entries, per-cell notes (bitmask), selected cell, notes mode, difficulty, seed, status ('playing'|'won')
Pure reducer `apply(state, action)` for actions: select, move (arrow direction, wraps), enter digit, erase, toggle note, toggle notes mode, new game
Givens cannot be changed; entering a digit clears that digit from peer notes
Tiny subscribe/getState/dispatch store in store.ts with no dependencies
status becomes 'won' when entries complete the grid without conflicts
Unit tests for every action

tasks.title: Notes, notes mode, new game action, and the store
acceptance: Adds actions: toggle note, toggle notes mode, new game; entering a digit clears that digit from peer notes

Unit tests for the new actions and the store

tasks.title: Undo and redo
acceptance: undo/redo actions over board-changing actions only (entries and notes, not selection)
A new edit after undo clears the redo stack; new game clears history
History is capped at 500 entries
Unit tests

tasks.title: Persistence: save and resume the current game and settings
acceptance: Saves game state (not undo history) to localStorage under a versioned key on every change, debounced
load() validates shape and version and returns null for missing or corrupt data instead of throwing
All storage access is wrapped in try/catch so private mode or blocked storage never breaks the game
Unit tests with a fake storage, including corrupt data

tasks.title: Timer and per-difficulty stats
acceptance: Elapsed time is tracked in state, pauses when the tab is hidden, and stops on win
Stats per difficulty: games started, games won, best time, average time; persisted like the game
Unit tests with an injected clock

tasks.title: Grid rendering with cell selection
acceptance: Renders a 9x9 grid with thick 3x3 box borders, givens styled differently from entries, and notes shown as a 3x3 mini grid
Clicking or tapping a cell selects it; selected cell, its row/column/box, and cells with the same digit are highlighted
Starts a generated medium puzzle on first load
Rendering subscribes to the store and updates only changed cells
Grid is square and fits a 360px-wide phone and a desktop window without scrolling
Colors are CSS custom properties on :root

tasks.title: Keyboard input

tasks.title: Number pad and controls bar for touch
acceptance: On-screen 1-9 pad that shows how many of each digit remain and disables completed digits
Buttons: erase, notes toggle (shows on/off), undo, redo
Touch targets at least 44px; layout stacks under the grid on narrow screens and beside it on wide ones

tasks.title: Conflict and mistake display
acceptance: Cells in conflict with a peer are marked (color plus a non-color cue such as an underline)
Setting 'show mistakes' (default off) additionally marks entries that disagree with the solution; stored with other settings

tasks.title: New game dialog with difficulty choice
acceptance: New Game button opens a native <dialog> with Easy/Medium/Hard/Expert
Asks for confirmation when a game is in progress
Puzzle generation runs without freezing the UI for more than 100 ms (use a Web Worker if needed)
On load, an in-progress saved game resumes instead of starting a new one

tasks.title: Win screen with time and stats
acceptance: On win: input stops, a dialog shows the time, difficulty and best time, with a New Game button
A timer is visible in the header during play and can be hidden in settings

tasks.title: Hint button
acceptance: Hint button highlights the cells involved and shows the explanation text; a second press applies the hint
Hints used are counted and shown on the win screen if T035 is merged, otherwise stored in state

tasks.title: Light/dark theme with a toggle
acceptance: Follows prefers-color-scheme by default; a toggle cycles system/light/dark and is persisted
All colors come from the :root custom properties; both themes meet WCAG AA contrast for digits
